subject: TTFT & streaming cadence — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@finedge.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: TTFT & streaming cadence — follow-up and next steps

Hi Samir / Anita,

Thanks again for the call today — great to learn more about FinEdge's real-time credit decisioning use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps focused on the performance items we discussed (TTFT + streaming cadence):

Summary of requirements you called out:
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) target: <= 80ms p50, <= 150ms p95 for 1-2 token initial response on short prompts (~32–64 tokens).
- Sustained throughput: ~400 reqs/sec at 1 concurrent request per user peak, with headroom for 2x burst concurrency during market open.
- Streaming: SSE or WebSocket acceptable. Chunk cadence preferred at ~40–100ms between chunks for progressive UI updates.
- Determinism: you need stable p95 under production traffic and graceful fallback to a slightly higher-latency tier if capacity constrained.

What I’ll send next (by EOD):
- Redwood TTFT benchmark summary (p50/p95 by model/instance type) — quick PDF.
- Suggested streaming chunk cadence guidance doc (small MD) showing examples for SSE and WebSocket and how chunk sizes affect perceived latency.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll attach the two docs mentioned above and a short config example for SSE/WebSocket streaming.
2) If the numbers look good, we can schedule a 30-minute deep-dive with one of our SREs to validate p95 behavior using a short replay of your production-ish traces (we can use a synthetic traffic profile).
3) Decisioning: mutual action plan & simple pilot (4–6 weeks) to validate TTFT at your peak load.

Are you ok with the targets summarized above? If so I’ll loop in our solutions engineer to book the SRE deep-dive.

Thanks,

—Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming cadence — follow-up and next steps

Marissa, thanks for the recap — that matches what we discussed. A few clarifying Qs from our side before we book the SRE session:

1) Can you confirm p95 TTFT numbers you’ve seen on the models we discussed (open LLM v2-family) on a single NVidia A10G-equivalent instance? We care about both cold-start and warm (with KV cache) scenarios.
2) For streaming chunk cadence: our UI is highly sensitive to the first few chunks — if we get initial chunk within <70ms we’re happy. Is that achievable with SSE?
3) For the pilot: what telemetry will you need from our side? We can provide traces and a small sample traffic replay, but want to know what formats you accept (OpenTelemetry, gzipped JSON, etc.).

If you can answer the above and share the docs you mentioned, we’ll confirm and book the deep-dive.

Best,
Samir
Head of Platform Engineering | FinEdge
samir@finedge.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@finedge.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming cadence — follow-up and next steps

Samir — thanks. See answers inline and attached docs (redwood-ttft-benchmarks-2026.pdf, streaming-chunk-cadence.md).

1) p95 TTFT numbers (high-level):
- Model: open-llm-v2-small on A10G-equivalent (single replica): p50 ~45ms, p95 ~120–140ms (warm, KV cache hit). Cold-start p95 can be ~300–600ms depending on kernel warms; we recommend keeping long-lived workers for production traffic to avoid cold-starts.
- Model: open-llm-v2-medium on A10G-equivalent: p50 ~60ms, p95 ~150–170ms (warm).
(See PDF for full matrix across instance types and multi-replica configurations.)

2) SSE/WebSocket chunk cadence:
- Yes, SSE can achieve initial chunk <70ms in our measurements if the model and worker are warm and the first chunk is small (1–8 tokens). We recommend: initial chunk size small (1–4 tokens), follow-up chunks every 40–80ms for good UX. The attached MD shows examples for implementing client-side buffering and latency smoothing.

3) Telemetry for pilot: we accept OpenTelemetry spans (OTLP/JSON), gzipped JSON traces, or plain logs — sample templates attached in the PDF appendix. For the SRE deep-dive we’ll ask for a small replay (5–10 minutes) and a traffic profile (RPS, concurrency, typical prompt length).

Next proposed step: Rishi will propose 2 times for a 30-min SRE session next week. If you can confirm availability, we’ll book and share a short agenda focused on: load profile, KB caches, streaming config, and expected p95 goals.

Cheers,
—Marissa
